t.2.1: Janaka said: Ah, I am stainless, tranquil, pure awareness, beyond nature. All this time I have been mocked by delusion alone.
t.2.2: Just as I alone illumine this body, so too do I illumine the world. Therefore the whole world is mine, or else nothing at all is mine.
t.2.3: Ah! Having now renounced the universe together with the body, I behold the Supreme Self through some skill alone.
t.2.4: Just as waves, foam and bubbles are not different from water, so the universe, which has emanated from the Self, is not different from the Self.
t.2.5: Just as a cloth, when examined, turns out to be nothing but thread, so this universe, when examined, is nothing but the Self alone.
t.2.6: Just as sugar, formed in the juice of the sugarcane, is wholly pervaded by that juice, so the universe, imagined in me, is pervaded by me through and through.
t.2.7: From ignorance of the Self the world appears; from knowledge of the Self it does not appear. From ignorance of the rope a snake appears; from knowledge of it, the snake indeed does not appear.
t.2.8: Light is my own true form; I am nothing other than that. When the universe shines forth, it is I alone who shine.
t.2.9: Ah! The universe, imagined through ignorance, appears in me, just as silver appears in mother-of-pearl, a snake in a rope, and water in the rays of the sun.
t.2.10: The universe that has come forth from me will dissolve back into me alone, just as a pot returns to clay, a wave to water, and a bracelet to gold.
t.2.11: Wonderful am I! Salutation to myself, for whom there is no destruction, who remain standing even when the world, from Brahmā down to a tuft of grass, is destroyed.
t.2.12: Wonderful am I! Salutations to myself! Though I possess a body, I am one; I neither go anywhere nor come from anywhere, but abide pervading the whole universe.
t.2.13: Wonderful am I! Salutations to myself! There is no one here as skilful as I, by whom this universe has long been upheld without ever touching it with the body.
t.2.14: Wonderful am I! Salutations to myself, to whom nothing at all belongs, or else to whom belongs everything that lies within the range of speech and mind.
t.2.15: Knowledge, the known, and likewise the knower: this triad does not truly exist. I am that Stainless One in whom this appears through ignorance.
t.2.17: I am pure awareness alone; out of ignorance I have imagined limiting adjuncts upon myself. Reflecting thus constantly, I abide in the changeless state beyond all mental constructs.
t.2.16: Ah, suffering is rooted in duality, and there is no other remedy for it than this: all this that is seen is false, and I am the One, the stainless essence of consciousness.
t.2.18: For me there is neither bondage nor liberation; delusion, having lost its support, has come to rest. Wonderful! The universe abides in me, yet in truth it does not abide in me.
t.2.20: The body, heaven and hell, bondage and liberation, and fear too, all this is mere imagination. What have I to do with any of it, I whose very self is pure consciousness?
t.2.19: It is certain that this universe, together with the body, is nothing at all, and the Self is pure consciousness alone; so in what could imagination now take hold?
t.2.21: Oh, even in a crowd of people, for me who sees no duality, it has become like a wilderness; where should I take delight?
t.2.22: I am not the body, nor is the body mine; I am not the individual soul, for I am pure consciousness. This alone was my bondage: the craving that I had for life.
t.2.23: Wonder! In me, the infinite great ocean, when the wind of the mind rises up, there is at once an upsurge of manifold waves of worlds.
t.2.24: When the wind of the mind grows calm in me, the infinite great ocean, the ship of the world, to the ill fortune of the hapless merchant that is the individual soul, is bound to perish.
t.2.25: How wonderful! In me, the boundless great ocean, the waves of individual souls by their very nature rise, strike one another, play, and sink back in.
